title: 30 Kinds of Rice Around the World
youtube_title: 30 Kinds of Rice Around the World
period_label: From sticky to fluffy, white to black
source_line: Sources: GI registers, FAO, IRRI, journals · Images: AI-generated
scope_note: 30 rice varieties and rice types, one per kind, ordered as a journey from East Asia west to the Americas. Not a ranking. Each card shows grain length (USDA classes: short, medium, long; extra-long = basmati-type slender grains), texture, colour and aroma. Flags show the growing country; basmati (India & Pakistan) and wild rice (USA & Canada) show both. All rice images are AI-generated illustrations. Wild rice is included as a famous 'rice' that is actually a different grass. Per-item sources are listed in the replies under the pinned comment.

insights.text: IRRI's genebank in the Philippines stores over 127,000 rice samples, the largest on Earth.
Glutinous rice is gluten-free: 'glutinous' means glue-like sticky, not gluten.
Sticky or fluffy? It's the starch: low-amylose rice clings, high-amylose rice stays apart.
Rice is the staple food for nearly half of the world's people.
Senegal's ceebu jën, UNESCO-listed in 2021, is made with fish and broken rice.
2004 World Food Prize: Yuan Longping (hybrid rice) and Monty Jones (NERICA, for Africa).

items.name: Koshihikari
items.subtitle: Niigata, Japan

source.name: Kobayashi et al. 2018, Breeding Science 68(2) (PMC5890008)

items.notes: Fact: Japan's most-planted rice every year since 1979, covering 36% of its paddy area in 2016. | Local name: コシヒカリ | Grain: Short grain (japonica); colour White; texture soft, glossy, slightly sticky. Sushi is not exclusive to Koshihikari; it is the archetypal Japanese short-grain table rice.

items.name: Yamada Nishiki
items.subtitle: Hyogo, Japan

source.name: Nippon.com, 'Yamadanishiki Reigns Supreme…' (3 Jul 2015)

items.notes: Fact: Developed in Hyogo in 1923. In 2014 Hyogo still grew 71% of Japan's crop of this sake rice. | Local name: 山田錦 | Grain: Large short grain, big starchy core; colour White (opaque heart); texture brewed, not eaten: milled down to its white core. Brewing rice: the 'dish' is the drink. 1923 = cross made; 1936 = name given (both in Nippon.com).

items.name: Mochigome
items.subtitle: Japan

source.name: Olsen & Purugganan 2002, Genetics 162: 941-950 (origin of glutinous rice)

items.notes: Fact: Glutinous rice has almost no amylose starch, which makes steamed, pounded mochi so sticky. | Local name: もち米 | Grain: Short grain, glutinous (waxy); colour Opaque white; texture very sticky, chewy, stretchy. Mochigome is a category (glutinous japonica), not one variety.

items.name: Wuchang Rice
items.subtitle: Heilongjiang, China

source.name: CNIPA (English), Wuchang Rice GI profile (24 Jul 2024)

items.notes: Fact: One of the first 100 Chinese GIs protected in the EU, under the EU-China deal signed in 2020. | Local name: 五常大米 | Grain: Short-medium grain (japonica); colour White; texture soft, glossy, slightly sticky. CNIPA: GI certification mark 2007; Wuyou/Songjing series varieties; ~130 frost-free days (one crop a year). 'Aromatic' refers to Wuyou (Daohuaxiang) types; name 'Daohuaxiang' not confirmed by CNIPA text, so not on card.

items.name: Zengcheng Simiao
items.subtitle: Guangdong, China

source.name: Rice journal 2023 (Guangdong Simiao grain standard: >6.5 mm, L/W >3.5)

items.notes: Fact: Simiao means 'silk seedling': Guangdong's standard demands grains over 3.5 times longer than wide. | Local name: 增城丝苗米 | Grain: Extra-long slender grain (indica); colour White, translucent; texture light, separate, springy grains. Claypot rice is the Cantonese showcase dish for long-grain simiao rice; the pairing is regional, not a protected recipe. 'Silk seedling' is a literal translation of 丝苗.

items.name: Pandan Wangi
items.subtitle: West Java, Indonesia

source.name: Jurnal Dharmakarya (Univ. Padjadjaran): Pandanwangi Cianjur, Kepmentan 163/2004 & IG

items.notes: Fact: Its name means 'fragrant pandan'. A local Javanese 'bulu' rice, released as a named variety in 2004. | Local name: Beras Pandan Wangi Cianjur | Grain: Medium-bold round grain (javanica 'bulu'); colour White; texture soft, fluffy, slightly sticky. IG date 16 Oct 2015 from one academic source; check DJKI register before publish. Nasi liwet = West Javanese (Sundanese) pairing, not variety-exclusive.

items.name: Broken Rice
items.subtitle: Mekong Delta, Vietnam

source.name: MICHELIN Guide Vietnam, 'What is com tam' (25 Jul 2023)

items.notes: Fact: Cracked grains were the cheap leftovers of milling; com tam turned them into Saigon's signature plate. | Local name: Gạo tấm | Grain: Broken fragments of long grain; colour White; texture soft, slightly dense, absorbs sauce. A processing grade, not a variety. On-screen text should use 'Com tam' if the font lacks Vietnamese diacritics.

items.name: Lao Sticky Rice
items.subtitle: Laos

source.name: IRRI Rice Today, Lao PDR and the International Rice Genebank

items.notes: Fact: Laos has deposited more than 15,000 rice samples in IRRI's genebank, the 2nd-largest national donation. | Local name: ເຂົ້າໜຽວ (khao niao) | Grain: Long/medium grain, glutinous; colour Opaque white; texture sticky, chewy, eaten by hand. IRRI field survey 1995-2000 (13,192 cultivated samples, 85.5% glutinous) supports 'most are sticky' if wanted on screen.

items.name: Thai Hom Mali
items.subtitle: Northeast Thailand

source.name: WIPO IP Advantage: Thai Hom Mali Rice from Thung Kula Rong-Hai

items.notes: Fact: The first Thai product registered as a GI in the EU (2013); named World's Best Rice in 2020 and 2021. | Local name: ข้าวหอมมะลิ | Grain: Long grain; colour White; texture soft, moist, slightly clingy. EU spec: KDML105 and RD15. WBR 2020/2021 source: https://www.thestar.com.my/aseanplus/aseanplus-news/2021/12/15/thai-hom-mali-rice-bags-worlds-best-rice-award-for-second-year-in-a-row . Green curry is a common pairing, not exclusive.

items.name: Riceberry
items.subtitle: Kasetsart University, Thailand

source.name: Rice Science Center, Kasetsart University: Riceberry

items.notes: Fact: Bred from 2002 at Kasetsart University by crossing purple Jao Hom Nin with jasmine rice KDML105. | Local name: ข้าวไรซ์เบอร์รี่ | Grain: Long slender grain (whole grain); colour Deep purple; texture soft but chewy, nutty. No single signature dish; eaten as whole-grain table rice. Big card text may be better as 'Purple rice'.

items.name: Paw San
items.subtitle: Ayeyarwady Delta, Myanmar

source.name: FFTC Agricultural Policy Platform: Paw San rice (Myanmar)

items.notes: Fact: Myanmar's 'pearl rice' was named World's Best Rice in 2011, beating Thai jasmine rice. | Local name: ပေါ်ဆန်းမွှေး | Grain: Short, plump grain that lengthens when cooked; colour White; texture soft, fluffy. FFTC page returned 403 to the fetcher; WBR 2011 also in Discourse/Rice Trader winner list and Irrawaddy. Re-open FFTC before publish.

items.name: Chak-hao
items.subtitle: Manipur, India

source.name: MyGov India blog: GI-tagged agricultural products of Manipur (GI app. 602)

items.notes: Fact: A fragrant, sticky black rice from Manipur; served at feasts as a deep-purple kheer. | Local name: Chak-hao (Meitei) | Grain: Medium grain, glutinous; colour Black (turns purple); texture sticky, soft. Name meaning ('delicious rice') only in Wikipedia, so kept off the card.

items.name: Gobindobhog
items.subtitle: West Bengal, India

source.name: S.S. Rana & Co.: Gobindobhog rice gets a GI tag (11 Jan 2018)

items.notes: Fact: Named after the offerings ('bhog') made to Govindajiu, family deity of Kolkata's Sett family. | Local name: গোবিন্দভোগ | Grain: Very short, round grain; colour White; texture slightly sticky, buttery. Payesh pairing: Gulf News / Kolkata food press (secondary).

items.name: Palakkadan Matta
items.subtitle: Kerala, India

source.name: ICAR KRISHI: 'Rice GIs of Kerala: Gap in Desired and Achieved Outcomes'

items.notes: Fact: Sold parboiled with its red bran on, so the chunky grains need a long soak and cook. | Local name: പാലക്കാടൻ മട്ട | Grain: Bold, coarse grain (parboiled); colour Red bran, pinkish; texture firm, chunky, earthy. GI registration date conflicting (Sep vs Nov 2007); kept off card. Parboiling detail from Wikipedia; ICAR record confirms GI. Sadya pairing is customary, not exclusive.

items.name: Jumli Marshi
items.subtitle: Jumla, Nepal

source.name: UNDP Nepal: Jumla's golden harvest and the revival of Marshi rice

items.notes: Fact: Grown at about 3,050 m in Chhumchaur, Jumla, which UNDP calls the highest rice cultivation on Earth. | Local name: जुम्ली मार्सी | Grain: Short-medium grain; colour Red; texture firm, nutty. Altitude conflicts: 3,050 m (UNDP, NepJOL) vs 2,850-2,900 m (2025 press, Tropentag). Card says 'about 3,050 m'; consider 'nearly 3,000 m' to be safe. Some sources say Marsi includes white/black types; red is the common form. Dal bhat = Nepal's everyday meal, not variety-exclusive.

items.name: Basmati
items.subtitle: Punjab, India & Pakistan

source.name: PIB / FSSAI press release: first regulatory standards for Basmati rice (12 Jan 2023)

items.notes: Fact: India's 2023 food standards require cooked basmati grains to average at least 12 mm long. | Local name: बासमती / باسمتی | Grain: Extra-long slender grain; colour White; texture fluffy, dry, separate grains. Shared India/Pakistan heritage and an ongoing GI dispute: flag chosen = IN (FSSAI rule is Indian); decide whether to show both flags or none. Do not claim one country 'owns' basmati.

items.name: Devzira
items.subtitle: Fergana Valley, Uzbekistan

source.name: Afisha.uz: Andijan devzira plov registered as a geographical indication (5 Jun 2026)

items.notes: Fact: In June 2026 Uzbekistan registered 'Andijan devzira plov' as a geographical indication. | Local name: Девзира / Devzira | Grain: Medium grain, ribbed; colour Reddish-pink tint; texture firm, holds shape, separate grains. Colour (reddish streak) sourced only to travel/trade pages; keep as visual descriptor, not a fact. Origin shared with Uzgen, Kyrgyzstan. Plov culture: UNESCO ICH 2016 (https://ich.unesco.org/en/RL/01166).

items.name: Hashemi
items.subtitle: Gilan, Iran

source.name: Tarang & Bakhshizadeh Gashti 2016, J. Integrative Agriculture (Hashemi genotypes)

items.notes: Fact: Persian cooks steam fragrant rice as chelow and prize tahdig, the golden crust at the pot's bottom. | Local name: برنج هاشمی | Grain: Long slender grain; colour White; texture fluffy, separate, elongates. Iranica page 403'd for the fetcher (content seen via search index). Hashemi = most-planted landrace in Gilan per Iranian papers; 'tahdig = bottom of the pot' is a literal translation.

items.name: Tosya Rice
items.subtitle: Kastamonu, Türkiye

source.name: TÜRKPATENT geographical indication No. 230 'Tosya Pirinci' (menşe adı)

items.notes: Fact: Ottoman records say rice from this valley was set aside for the Sultan's table. | Local name: Tosya Pirinci (Sarıkılçık) | Grain: Medium grain; colour White (reddish-yellow husk); texture tender, separate grains for pilav. Registry text: 'padişah hassı (sofrası)'; also Turkey's first rice mill in Tosya, 1926. Registered 08.11.2017, protected from 12.11.2014. Continent: Anatolia = Asia.

items.name: Carnaroli
items.subtitle: Vercelli & Pavia, Italy

source.name: Città di Paullo press release: 80th anniversary of Carnaroli rice (2025)

items.notes: Fact: Created in 1945 by crossing Vialone and Lencino; its firm grains hold their shape in risotto. | Local name: Riso Carnaroli | Grain: Large medium-long grain; colour Pearly white core; texture creamy outside, firm 'al dente' core. Riso di Baraggia Biellese e Vercellese PDO (Reg. CE 982/2007) covers Carnaroli among others; Carnaroli itself is not a PDO. 'History not well defined' per Wikipedia; 1945 cross is the consensus date.

items.name: Camargue Red
items.subtitle: Rhône Delta, France

source.name: CooksInfo: Camargue red rice

items.notes: Fact: Developed by a Camargue farming family with INRA in the 1980s; first harvested in 1988. | Local name: Riz rouge de Camargue | Grain: Short-medium grain (wholegrain); colour Red-brown; texture chewy, nutty, slightly sticky. Origin details (1982 vs 1983 discovery, 'chance cross') conflict between CooksInfo and Provence7; card only uses the shared points (1980s, INRA, 1988 harvest). Dish is a generic serving; consider 'Red rice' as big text instead.

items.name: Calasparra Bomba
items.subtitle: Calasparra, Spain

source.name: Interreg Europe SME Origin: The rice of Calasparra PDO

items.notes: Fact: Rice from the mountains of Calasparra in Murcia has held a Designation of Origin since 1986. | Local name: Arroz de Calasparra (Bomba) | Grain: Short, round grain; colour Pearly white; texture absorbent, grains stay whole. Spanish order 19 Feb 1986 (BOE 4 Mar 1986). 'First rice DO in Spain/world' is repeated by retailers/tourism only, so not used. PDO varieties: Bomba and Balilla x Sollana.

items.name: Carolino
items.subtitle: Ribatejo, Portugal

source.name: Observador / Lusa, data from ANIA (13 Mar 2023)

items.notes: Fact: Portugal eats about 16 kg of rice per person a year, the most in Europe and 4x the EU average. | Local name: Arroz Carolino | Grain: Medium-long grain (japonica); colour White; texture creamy, soaks up broth. 16 kg = white rice, ANIA 2023; other years cite 15-18 kg.

items.name: Egyptian Rice
items.subtitle: Nile Delta, Egypt

source.name: FAO: Rice in Egypt, general information (Giza/Sakha varieties)

items.notes: Fact: Unusually for Africa, most Egyptian rice varieties are japonica, grown almost all in the Nile Delta. | Local name: أرز مصري | Grain: Short-medium grain (japonica); colour White; texture soft, slightly sticky. 'Unusually for Africa' is a framing; FAO states japonica + Lower Nile only. Mahshi pairing is customary.

items.name: Ofada Rice
items.subtitle: Ogun State, Nigeria

source.name: Gyimah-Brempong, Johnson & Takeshima 2016, The Nigerian Rice Economy (UPenn Press), pp. 30-31

items.notes: Fact: Often a blend that includes African rice, sold unpolished with bran left on; brown Ofada is very aromatic. | Local name: Ìrẹsì Ofada | Grain: Short-medium grain, unpolished; colour Brown-red or white; texture firm, chewy, swells when cooked. URL is the Wikipedia page citing the book; the book itself was not opened. Replace with a direct book or NCRI/WARDA source before publish.

items.name: African Rice
items.subtitle: Inner Niger Delta, Mali

source.name: AfricaRice: birthplace of African rice domestication identified in Mali

items.notes: Fact: A separate species from Asian rice, domesticated about 3,000 years ago in Mali's Inner Niger Delta. | Local name: Oryza glaberrima | Grain: Medium grain; colour Reddish bran; texture firm, nutty. SURPRISE: not Oryza sativa. No single signature dish found in sources (used in Ofada blends; ceremonial for the Jola of Casamance). Big card text could be 'A rice of its own' instead.

items.name: Brazilian Long-Grain
items.subtitle: Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil

source.name: Brasil de Fato citing Conab forecast for 2024/25 (15 Oct 2024)

items.notes: Fact: Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil's southernmost state, grows about 70% of the country's rice. | Local name: Arroz agulhinha | Grain: Long, thin grain; colour White; texture loose, separate grains. 'Agulhinha' is the market name for long-fine rice; no source opened for the term. 70% is a Conab estimate (other years 70-72%). 'Largest producer outside Asia' was not cleanly sourced, so not used.

items.name: Morelos Rice
items.subtitle: Morelos, Mexico

source.name: Redalyc (2023): local agri-food system and the Arroz del Estado de Morelos DO

items.notes: Fact: Mexico's rice DO (2012) protects INIFAP's Morelos A-92, A-98 and A-2010, with their chalky 'white belly'. | Local name: Arroz del Estado de Morelos | Grain: Large, extra-long grain; colour White with opaque 'white belly'; texture soft, absorbent, holds sauce. DOF publication 16 Feb 2012; NOM-080-SCFI-2016. 'Panza blanca' description from IPN thesis + press.

items.name: Carolina Gold
items.subtitle: South Carolina, USA

source.name: The Post and Courier, 'Saving Carolina Gold: The first revival' (14 Dec 2025)

items.notes: Fact: Revived in 1986 from 14 lb of seed kept by a USDA lab in Texas; by 1988 the harvest was 10,000 lb. | Local name: Carolina Gold | Grain: Long grain (heirloom); colour White (golden hull); texture tender, creamy-starchy. Grown by enslaved Africans in the Lowcountry; handle respectfully. Hoppin' John link: chef Sean Brock's claim (Wikipedia), so it is a pairing, not a fact.

items.name: Wild Rice
items.subtitle: Great Lakes, USA & Canada

source.name: Minnesota Secretary of State: State Grain - Wild Rice

items.notes: Fact: Not true rice: Zizania is an aquatic grass. Minnesota made it the state grain in 1977. | Local name: Manoomin (Ojibwe) | Grain: Very long, needle-like seed; colour Dark brown to black; texture chewy, splits open when cooked. SURPRISE / caveat card: genus Zizania (tribe Oryzeae), not Oryza. Traditionally harvested from canoes; Ojibwe cultural significance.
